newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebel leader to intervene in refugee crisis.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebel leader to intervene in refugee crisis.

text.p: Rebel leader Laurent Kabila sent aides to northeastern Zaire on Saturday before flying in to face U.N. aid agency outrage at the fate of nearly 100,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees missing in thick jungle.
The row over the treatment of refugees scattered from at least two camps south of the northeastern capital Kisangani is the biggest international crisis for Kabila's seven-month rebellion.
Senior officials of his Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (AFDL) left Lubumbashi to prepare for their leader's arrival by plane later on Saturday.
"It is a mission to gather first-hand information on what is happening there with regards to the refugees," an official said.

U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan has called rebel treatment of the refugees this week "slow extermination", and a U.N. food agency spokeswoman, making a comparison with Hitler's Germany, has said: "The expression 'Final Solution' is not exaggerated."
Kabila told Reuters he would go to Kisangani from Zaire's second city Lubumbashi to direct a hands-on investigation.
"The visit of Kabila will provide us with the opportunity to take up his offer of access to U.N. agencies and to seek an overall solution," said U.N. refugee agency UNHCR spokesman Paul Stromberg.
Stromberg said Kabila was expected to meet Aldo Aiello, the European Union special envoy to the Great Lakes region, and Pierce Gerety, U.N. humanitarian coordinator for the region.
He said aid agencies would send teams to places where the AFDL gave access but rebels had said security from km seven (mile four) to km 82 (mile 50) south of Kisangani was not good enough.
He said a train was being loaded with medical supplies and aid for the town of Ubundu, 100 km (60 miles) south, and aid workers would fly to km 95 (mile 59) on an evaluation mission.
"We have received a report that refugees are arriving in Ubundu but we don't know from where and how many," he added.

Kabila has forecast a swift battle for the capital Kinshasa as a rift has developed over venues for face-to-face talks with ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko. At the same time, the government has accused Angola of invading to the west of the capital as it faced rebel advances to the east.
State radio on Friday quoted the presidency as saying thousands of traders and residents fled Yema village, close to Muanda on the Atlantic coast and 400 km (250 miles) west of Kinshasa.
The statement said the village was invaded early this week by 1,400 heavily armed soldiers of the Angolan army. Angolan troops were also around Tshikapa, further inland, it said.
The commander of the elite presidential guard (DSP) railed at his troops to "fight to your death" to defend Mobutu and the nation. The army has done more looting than fighting so far.
Kabila said he was looking for a solution to the problem of the refugees, the rump of two million who fled Rwanda in 1994 fearing reprisals for genocide of Tutsis and Hutu moderates.

Some 85,000 refugees abandoned two refugee camps south of Kisangani this week after fighting at both sites and disappeared into the jungle, where aid workers fear thousands who were already malnourished and very sick will soon perish.
"I am for a clean and independent investigation into this whole saga. I seek and demand the truth only," Kabila said.
Kabila, whose forces control about half of Africa's third largest and perhaps potentially richest nation, invited the United Nations to send in an independent investigation team.
But he added large numbers of the refugees were Hutu former Rwandan troops and militiamen "still armed to their teeth and using the refugee cause to hide their criminal activities".

Kabila said his rebels were disciplined but he was willing to punish any found guilty of "excesses" although "so far the facts before me suggest my troops only intervened to stop fighting between heavily armed refugees and local Zaireans".
Aid workers say they fear rebels regard all Hutu refugees hiding in the jungle as former Rwandan troops and militiamen guilty of genocide or their dependents and show little mercy.
